metadata.title: मेगा ग्रेट निकोबार प्रोजेक्ट और शोम्पेन आदिवासी | Great Nicobar Project And Shompen Tribe
metadata.description: This explainer focuses on the Great Nicobar development project and its environmental concerns. The Indian government has planned four large-scale infrastructure projects in the ecologically sensitive Great Nicobar Island, including an international container terminal, an airport, and power plants. However, the development threatens the island’s rich tropical rainforest, home to diverse plant and animal species, including the indigenous Shompen tribe. The project requires clearing significant forest areas, with estimates suggesting that between 9.64 lakh and 32 lakh trees may be felled. The explainer highlights the complex ecology of the island, concerns raised by environmentalists and scientists, and the ongoing political debate regarding the project's impact. While compensatory afforestation is planned in Haryana's Aravalli range, experts argue that this cannot replace the unique biodiversity of the Great Nicobar. This piece emphasizes the balance between national development interests and the need to protect irreplaceable natural habitats.
